notes: §1985:VIII.2.3.4 GR1 requires 'all file control entries in the run unit which reference this file connector' to have the same OPTIONAL phrase, a consistent ASSIGN, the same RESERVE integer, organization, access mode and RELATIVE KEY external item. ExternalFileConnectorRules.Check (BinderDriver, every edition) compares each entry's FileEntryIdentity.Segments with the first describer's (COBOL6847) and requires the RELATIVE KEY item external and the same in each entry (COBOL1624/COBOL1575, §1985:VIII.2.4.4 GR8); the FILE STATUS sameness it asks only at 2023 (is2023), so 85 keeps per-entry status items. Probes at --std 85 on a two-program run unit with an EXTERNAL relative file: identical entries with different non-external FILE STATUS items run (SUB READ ALPHA; refused COBOL1624/1573 at 2023); OPTIONAL dropped, ASSIGN "OTHERF", RESERVE 3 vs 2, RESERVE omitted vs 2, ACCESS DYNAMIC vs RANDOM and ORGANIZATION SEQUENTIAL each refused COBOL6847 naming the clause; RELATIVE KEY RK2 (other external item) refused COBOL1575, a non-external RK3 COBOL1624+1575; after a failed OPEN INPUT (status 35) the subprogram's READ gives status 47 and no INVALID KEY. Separately compiled describers that differ run unchecked unless EC checking is on (ExternalTable.Describe); 1985 states no detection duty for this general rule. Witness: matching entries share the connector.

next.reason: §2023:12.4.5.3 GR1 keeps 1985 a)-f) (OPTIONAL, ASSIGN consistency, RESERVE, organization, access mode, RELATIVE KEY external item) but adds requirements, among them 'i) The same specification of the FILE STATUS clause, where data-name-4 shall reference the same corresponding external data item', also stated in §2023:14.8.4.2. 1985 allowed different status items per entry: 'The data item referenced by data-name-1 which is updated ... is the one specified in the file control entry associated with that statement' (§1985:VII.2.5.4 GR2). A 1985 program whose entries for one external file name different or no FILE STATUS items is no longer conforming (stricter); l) sharing and m) lock mode add further consistency requirements.
